visual_argument: Tesla's own Texas capacity table walked as a plant at night: every bay whose row reads Production has its line lit, and the Optimus bay, whose row reads Construction with no figure, is a dark slab of anchor bolts, taped empty pads and crated tools under two work lamps, with its high bay lamps present and off. Two plan reliefs carry the figures the doors can't, at one scale each.
build_risk: Frame 5 is an interior with no robot in it: a TXT.interior bay 24 by 30 m with the open door as its only key opening, four chassis models (anchor_bolt_set, tool_crate, tripod_work_lamp, high bay fixture rows switched off) and three kit machine_pads in bluebonnet tape. A dark slab as the largest shape is a charge the judges have made before, so the bolts are built close and large with threads that catch the flood, their casts own the lower third, and the crates carry plywood grain and steel strapping. If one repair fails, the camera moves onto the apron looking in through the door, the bolts and tape seen across the threshold with sky over the parapet.
distinct_from_recent: No. 58 (Oct 23) was a lastLight still life of bone cards and ember tape on a shale ledge at hand distance. No. 57 (Oct 22) was a lastLight stair of limestone and weathering steel on caliche. No. 56 (Oct 21) was lastLight machine shop rooms with plan reliefs of trays. This deck is a floodlit night exterior at plant scale, tilt up walls, steel and a sealed apron under one cold LED flood from camera left at az -58 el 25, with bluebonnet tape as the only accent meaning planned or under construction, and no still life, no room built as a set piece except the one bay the claim is about.
